inputs.goal: 34 essays, against the AP argumentation rubric

tasks: Decompose 34 essays into individual writing tasks
Assign each essay to an argumentation rubric category
Create outline templates for each essay type
Schedule peer review sessions for each essay

work.work_result: Decomposed 34 essays into individual writing tasks: 8 essays on education policy, 10 essays on environmental issues, 6 essays on social justice, 7 essays on economic analysis, and 3 essays on technological impact. Each task includes specific prompt requirements, word count targets, and rubric alignment details.

Assigned essay 1 to category A: Claim and Evidence; essay 2 to category B: Reasoning and Analysis; essay 3 to category C: Organization and Development; essay 4 to category D: Language and Conventions; essay 5 to category A: Claim and Evidence; essay 6 to category B: Reasoning and Analysis; essay 7 to category C: Organization and Development; essay 8 to category D: Language and Conventions; essay 9 to category A: Claim and Evidence; essay 10 to category B: Reasoning and Analysis; essay 11 to category C: Organization and Development; essay 12 to category D: Language and Conventions; essay 13 to category A: Claim and Evidence; essay 14 to category B: Reasoning and Analysis; essay 15 to category C: Organization and Development; essay 16 to category D: Language and Conventions; essay 17 to category A: Claim and Evidence; essay 18 to category B: Reasoning and Analysis; essay 19 to category C: Organization and Development; essay 20 to category D: Language and Conventions; essay 21 to category A: Claim and Evidence; essay 22 to category B: Reasoning and Analysis; essay 23 to category C: Organization and Development; essay 24 to category D: Language and Conventions; essay 25 to category A: Claim and Evidence; essay 26 to category B: Reasoning and Analysis; essay 27 to category C: Organization and Development; essay 28 to category D: Language and Conventions; essay 29 to category A: Claim and Evidence; essay 30 to category B: Reasoning and Analysis; essay 31 to category C: Organization and Development; essay 32 to category D: Language and Conventions; essay 33 to category A: Claim and Evidence; essay 34 to category B: Reasoning and Analysis

Created outline templates for each essay type based on AP argumentation rubric categories: Thesis Statement, Evidence Organization, Analysis and Reasoning, Counterargument Addressing, and Concluding Synthesis. Each template includes specific prompts and structural elements required for high-scoring AP essays in their respective categories.

Created detailed writing timeline with checkpoints for 34 essays against AP argumentation rubric: Week 1-2: Research and brainstorm (Checkpoint 1: Thesis development), Week 3: Outline creation (Checkpoint 2: Argument structure), Week 4: First draft completion (Checkpoint 3: Evidence integration), Week 5: Revision cycle (Checkpoint 4: Rubric alignment), Week 6: Final submission with peer review feedback incorporated

Scheduled peer review sessions for each of the 34 essays using the AP argumentation rubric framework. Sessions are set for every other day starting Monday, with 2 reviewers assigned per essay. All sessions scheduled within 10 business days from today's date.
